Europe in 1453: the year a capital that had stood for over a thousand years fell. Look at who surrounds it on this map.

a thread 🧵🗺️
1/ Constantinople fell on 29 May 1453, after a 53-day siege that began on 6 April. The Ottoman sultan, Mehmed II, was only in his early twenties.
2/ The numbers were lopsided. Defenders totalled about 7,000, roughly 2,000 of them foreigners. Recent estimates put the Ottoman army at 50,000 to 80,000.

3/ The Theodosian walls had protected the city for about 800 years. Gunpowder artillery finally broke them, including a giant cannon cast by Orban that could throw a stone ball weighing around 270 kg over a mile.
4/ The last emperor, Constantine XI Palaiologos, died in the final assault. His exact fate is unknown, though he is said to have fought in the streets.
5/ Mehmed made Constantinople his capital, replacing Edirne. Notice how the Ottoman Empire already fills the Balkans on the map, with Serbia, Bosnia and Wallachia as the remaining buffers.
6/ In the far northeast sits Muscovy. The same year, a Tver writer was already calling Moscow heir to fallen Rome, an idea that grew into the 'Third Rome'. We'll map that claim next.
Is 1453 the end of the Middle Ages for you? Follow @forummapping for more maps like this.
